<thought>Based on the molecular formula C5H8O2, DBE = 2, one carbonyl group, and no methyl groups, the most plausible structure is a cyclopentanone bearing a single hydroxyl substituent. This satisfies the ring (1 DBE) plus carbonyl (1 DBE). The SMILES for 3‑hydroxycyclopentan‑2‑one (or any mono‑hydroxy cyclopentanone) is `O=C1CC(O)CC1`. This string is a valid SMILES representation of the molecule.</thought>
<final_answer>O=C1CC(O)CC1</final_answer>
